name: Who's In?
tagline: With you it feels like a party. It's also going somewhere.
epigraph: A bartending school went bust. Its party bar didn't. This glass is that bar's size.
glassware: a big glass (about 400 ml, a 14-oz highball or double old-fashioned), chilled in the freezer, packed with crushed ice and a straw
language_row: Wren's checks on v3: whoYouAre 181 words, yours 502, history 48% of yours, epigraph 15 words; 4-grams of epigraph, whoYouAre and every yours paragraph clean against every pour file and the registry; y5 and the closing line share no 4-gram; no he/she/we/our or bare "yours" in guest text (lint: 0 warnings). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/lab-london-academy-of-bartenders.md`. *A Proper Drink* (Simonson), pp. 97–101, reliable secondary (participants on the record). Oxford Companion, ANKRAH, DOUGLAS (pdf 119), primary. *The Spirits Business*, 17 Aug 2021, web, secondary. *Cocktail Codex* p. 134 (the built Mojito method). *Liquid Intelligence* pp. 44, 81. *The Flavor Matrix*, berry entry (pdf 52): cumin as a surprise pairing.
names_note: *Who's In?* (all three, round 5), over *Change of Plan* (Wren's v1 pick, which Tomás took up in round 4 as Wren moved to *Who's In?*, the names crossing), *Best Idea Yet*, *Along for It* and *Right Then*.
open_items: Hester's optional wording note on the epigraph, not taken: read cold, "This glass is that bar's size." can parse as the size of the bar itself; her alternative "Its glasses were this big." changes no fact. Wren's call; Robin may prefer it.
New ingredient rows this room (Tomás's numbers): raspberry_syrup, raspberry_cumin_syrup, raspberry_fresh, mint_leaves_left_in.

The raspberry is the room's choice (LAB's backbar was "like a greengrocer"), said as "I chose"; the cumin is the Flavor Matrix's berry-family surprise pairing, not raspberry by name. *Worth the Trip* also uses cumin, in a different cocktail.
The jiggers stay out of guest text (contested, *Proper* p. 100); the 14-oz glass line is Turner's, and he left before the bar opened, so the glass is cited, not his voice.
